record.what_it_does: Cloudflare is a global network platform offering CDN, DNS, security (WAF/Zero Trust), and serverless compute (Workers, R2, D1) products, all controllable via a single REST/GraphQL API.
record.auth_notes: Cloudflare's primary and recommended credential is a scoped 'API Token' passed as a Bearer token in the Authorization header; a legacy account-wide 'Global API key' is also supported but discouraged. OAuth2 is documented specifically for authorizing third-party/MCP clients to act on a user's behalf against the API (e.g. Cloudflare's own remote MCP servers use an OAuth redirect flow), while direct REST API automation typically uses API tokens.
record.access_notes: Any developer can sign up for a free Cloudflare account and immediately create an API Token from the dashboard to call the API — no approval or paid plan required for core API access. Some downstream features (e.g. webhook delivery for Notifications) are gated to Professional/Business plans, but that is a product-feature gate, not an API-access gate.
